edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Regular oral exposure in infancy may train immune tolerance at a window when withholding peanut leaves sensitization more likely.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2016 Ierodiakonou meta analysis in JAMA, which ties early peanut introduction to peanut allergy in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
